title: BNCI 2015-012 PASS2D P300 dataset
description: This dataset comprises preprocessed EEG recordings from a novel 9-class auditory event-related potential (ERP) paradigm designed for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. Ten healthy participants performed a spelling task using a predictive text entry system (PASS2D) that exploited spatial auditory stimuli varying in pitch and direction. The dataset includes 63-channel EEG data sampled at 250 Hz with P300 and N200 components, along with performance metrics demonstrating competitive spelling speeds of 0.8 characters per minute.
methods_description: Data were acquired from 10 healthy participants in a single session consisting of a calibration phase (3 runs with 9 trials each) and an online spelling phase (2 runs). EEG was recorded from 63 electrodes using wet Ag/AgCl electrodes in a 10-20 montage at 250 Hz sampling rate with nose reference. Auditory stimuli (708, 524, 380 Hz tones) were presented via headphones in a 9-class paradigm varying in pitch and spatial direction. Preprocessing included analog bandpass filtering (0.1-250 Hz), digital lowpass filtering (40 Hz), downsampling to 100 Hz, and artifact rejection (peak-to-peak voltage >100 μV). Classification used linear Fisher discriminant analysis with shrinkage regularization on mean amplitudes from discriminative intervals (N200: 230-300 ms, P300: 350+ ms).
